publisher: ENTSO-E (European Network of Transmission System Operators for Electricity)
title: Expert Panel Final Report on the 28 April 2025 Iberian Blackout
date_evidence: news ENTSO-E Publishes Expert Panel Final Report on 28 April 2025 Blackout in Spain and Portugal 20 March 2026
key_claim: The 28 April 2025 Iberian blackout resulted from many interacting factors - oscillations, gaps in voltage and reactive power control, differences in voltage regulation practices, rapid output reductions and generator disconnections; the panel's recommendations stress voltage and reactive-power control, oscillatory stability and adapting regulatory frameworks to the evolving power system.
notes: Tier 1 primary investigation; reframes the binding reliability problem from adequacy to dynamic stability/voltage control.

title: Electricity 2026 - Analysis and forecast to 2030
date_evidence: the IEA "Electricity 2026" report was published on 06 February 2026
key_claim: As the share of synchronous generators declines, system strength can be reinforced by deploying grid-forming inverters and installing synchronous condensers; over 2,500 GW of projects are stalled in grid queues worldwide and annual grid investment must rise about 50% by 2030 from USD 400 billion; blackouts in Chile, the Iberian Peninsula and Mexico in 2025 had widespread impacts.
notes: Structural anchor - canonical global framing of system strength and grid-forming inverters. ~4 months old.

title: New contracts awarded under the Mid-Term (Y-1) Stability Market Round 2
date_evidence: Balancing services 24 Feb 2026 - 1 minute read ... secure 7.3 GVA.s of inertia between October 2026 to September 2027
key_claim: NESO awarded five contracts across four providers to secure 7.3 GVA.s of inertia (October 2026-September 2027) under the Mid-Term (Y-1) Stability Market at an estimated cost of GBP 10.3 million, expected to deliver up to GBP 44.4 million in consumer savings; enduring stability markets were launched in 2023 to procure inertia as a traded service.
notes: Concrete evidence that inertia/system strength is now procured through dedicated markets.

title: Grid-forming, hybrids and alternative chemistries in Wood Mackenzie's 2026 energy storage trend predictions
key_claim: Global variable-renewable penetration reached about 36% of installed electricity capacity in 2025 and is projected to climb to 56% by 2035; high penetration has stressed synchronous grids, making grid-forming storage a critical component for system stability; ENTSO-E has published technical requirements to harmonise grid-forming capability, with formal regulation expected in 2026 - a shift from voluntary adoption to mandated integration.
notes: Wood Mackenzie consultancy analysis (Tier 2) cited via trade press; names the voluntary-to-mandated regulatory shift.

publisher: National Renewable Energy Laboratory (reported via pv magazine)
title: Grid-forming inverters significantly enhance grid stability - NREL Kaua'i analysis
key_claim: NREL testing on Kaua'i found that grid-forming inverter-based resources significantly enhance grid stability; after the utility switched to grid-forming controls to provide synthetic inertia, a 2023 generator trip produced no oscillation, unlike a comparable 2021 event when grid-following inverters caused frequency oscillations.
notes: National-laboratory research (Tier 2) reported via pv magazine; efficacy evidence for grid-forming inverters.

title: Combination of voltage and oscillation caused Iberian blackout, says ENTSO-E report
key_claim: ENTSO-E's final report identified at least 15 interacting factors and issued 23 recommendations (13 tied to root causes); ENTSO-E president Damian Cortinas said renewables were not the problem, voltage control was; Spain's Operational Procedure 7.4, allowing renewables to contribute to voltage control, was fully implemented on 17 March 2026.
notes: Tier 3 journalism corroborating ENTSO-E; supplies the OP 7.4 regulatory-response data point.

title: Wood Mackenzie highlights growing grid stability risks as coal and gas plants retire and synchronous condensers return to focus
key_claim: Large synchronous machines supplied inertia, fault (short-circuit) current and reactive power automatically through their own physics; as inverter-based resources replace them this built-in support disappears just as AI data-centre loads can swing by hundreds of MW within seconds; inertia is treated inconsistently across jurisdictions - the UK recognises it as a paid service while Sweden treats it as free.
notes: Tier 3 trade press relaying Wood Mackenzie/ABB; supplies the byproduct-disappearing framing and the pay-vs-free contrast.
